title: Caller ID Trust Research for Customer Support Decisions
excerpt: A source-bounded study of caller-ID trust boundaries, evidence limits, adverse controls, and accountable decisions in offshore support.
methodology: This report maps ten authoritative public sources to one operational question about caller-ID trust boundaries. It defines the observation unit before collection, uses ordinary and adverse synthetic controls, preserves missing evidence, requires an independently reviewed subset, and separates observed events from interpretation. Sources were checked on October 12, 2026.
limitations: This is a design and evidence review, not legal advice, certification, a provider benchmark, or proof of causation. Results remain bounded to the named queue, period, systems, definitions, records, and reviewer access. Laws, standards, carrier behavior, and product interfaces can change; the fraud and customer-security owner must confirm the current requirement before release.
keyTakeaways: displayed caller information can support routing but should not independently authorize disclosure, recovery, or account change
Test caller-ID trust boundaries with adverse as well as ordinary cases.
Keep consequential decisions with the fraud and customer-security owner.
